The '''6th Academy Awards''' were held on March 16, 1934, to honor films released between August 1, 1932, and December 31, 1933, at [[Ambassador Hotel (Los Angeles)|The Ambassador Hotel]] in Los Angeles, California.  They were hosted by [[Will Rogers]], who also presented the awards.

When Rogers presented [[Academy Award for Best Director|Best Director]], he opened the envelope and simply announced, "Come up and get it, Frank!" [[Frank Capra]], certain he was the winner, ran to the podium to collect the Oscar, only to discover Rogers had meant [[Frank Lloyd]], who had won for ''Cavalcade''. Rogers then called the third nominee, [[George Cukor]], to join the two Franks on stage.<ref name=McBride>McBride, Joseph, ''Frank Capra: The Catastrophe of Success''. New York: Simon & Schuster 1992. {{ISBN|0-671-73494-6}}, pp. 288–292, 294–296, 298–302, 309–310</ref><ref name="Oscars '33 Notes">{{cite book |last1=Wallechinsky |first1=David |last2=Wallace |first2=Irving |date=1975 |title=The People's Almanac |url=https://archive.org/details/peoplesalmanac00wall/page/832/mode/2up |location=Garden City, New York |publisher=Doubleday & Company, Inc. |page=833 |isbn=0-385-04060-1}}</ref> After this, he summoned two of the Best Actress nominees—[[Diana Wynyard]] and [[May Robson]]—to the stage. Although they both thought they won in a tie, Rogers thanked them for their performances before announcing the actual winner: [[Katharine Hepburn]].<ref name="Oscars '33 Notes"/> 

A change in the eligibility rules resulted in the longest time frame for which films could be nominated: the seventeen months from August 1, 1932, to December 31, 1933. After this, the eligibility period would coincide with the calendar year. This resulted in the only time no ceremony was held in a calendar year (1933).<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Feinberg|first=Scott|date=June 15, 2020|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/awards/oscars-pushed-back-eligibility-window-extended-9402751/|title=Oscars Pushed Back to April 25, Eligibility Window Extended|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|access-date=June 18, 2026}}</ref>

This was the last time that no film had more than four nominations, as well as the only year in Academy history in which no film other than the Best Picture nominees received multiple nominations. ''Cavalcade'' became the fourth film to win Best Picture without a writing nomination, and the last until ''[[Hamlet (1948 film)|Hamlet]]'' (1948) at the [[21st Academy Awards]].

[[Walt Disney]] became the first person to win consecutive Academy Awards, winning Best Short Subject, Cartoon for ''The [[Three Little Pigs (film)|Three Little Pigs]]'' after having won the same award [[5th Academy Awards|the previous year]] for ''[[Flowers and Trees]]''.

This was the first time in the Academy's history that both of the major acting nominees were absent from the big night.<ref name="Oscars '33 Notes"/>
